title: Selling the gate to public service
news: A former KPSC chairman, accused of leaking answer keys for bribes, was also suspended over the commission's recruitment of his own daughter.
syllabus: Probity in governance; Integrity; Conflict of interest; Impartiality
link: A recruiting body is the gate to public service: when its head sells answer keys and selects his own daughter, it betrays the impartiality and trust on which the whole civil service rests. Corruption at the entry point corrupts every service that follows.
question: "Corruption in public recruitment is the most damaging form of corruption because it corrupts the system at its source." Discuss.

title: Dollar investors, rupee investors
news: Amid calls to cut taxes for foreign investors, the Finance Minister asked: 'If you pitch for dollar investors, what about rupee investors?'
syllabus: Impartiality and non-partisanship; Fairness in public policy
link: Public policy must treat like cases alike: concessions that favour foreign over domestic investors for the same income break fairness and impartiality, even when the aim of attracting capital is legitimate. Good ends do not justify unequal means.
question: "Fairness in public policy means treating like cases alike." Examine with an example from economic policy.

title: Governing on trust
news: The Finance Minister said GST, income tax and other policies are framed on trusting businesses, farmers, taxpayers and citizens: 'That will remain our charter.'
syllabus: Public service values; Trust and citizen-centric governance; Accountability
link: A state that presumes honesty treats citizens as partners, not suspects, cutting harassment and compliance costs. Trust must be paired with accountability, so that honest citizens are freed while the few who abuse trust still face consequences.
question: "Trust-based governance must be balanced with accountability." Discuss with examples.

title: Anticipate, but with care
news: CERT-In is testing an advanced AI model to find software flaws before attackers do, but only on small datasets, wary of exposing sensitive public data.
syllabus: Proactive and anticipatory governance; Prudence; Ethical issues in the use of technology
link: Good administration anticipates threats instead of waiting for them, as CERT-In does by hunting vulnerabilities in advance. Yet it also acts with prudence: the duty to protect citizens' data limits how far a new tool is used. Proactivity with caution is responsible governance.
question: "Proactive governance requires both foresight and prudence." Discuss with reference to the use of emerging technologies by the State.

title: The State's duty to be knowable
news: A writer proposes that only rules published on one national legal register should be enforceable against citizens.
syllabus: Transparency; Rule of law; Probity in governance; Trust
link: A government that enforces rules citizens cannot find betrays fairness; publishing every obligation is an ethical duty that limits discretion and corruption.
question: "Hidden rules are the soil in which corruption grows." Discuss.
